title: Pompeii: The Last Song of Vesuvius
subtitle: Save the people. The mountain cannot be saved.

authors.role: game design, programming, pixel art, music
authors.name: AI coding agents (Claude Code by Anthropic, and others) under the project lead's direction

acknowledgements: Pompeii and the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79 are history; Livia, the citizens and the Sibylline society are fiction.
The tibia is an attested Roman double pipe; its magic is invented.
All art, text and music are original: low-poly models and districts drawn by a fixed-point software 3D renderer, a 3x5 font and melodies written for this game.
Gameplay is inspired by late-1990s third-person 3D action-adventures; no characters, art, music, names or interface from any existing game are used.
Edward Bulwer-Lytton's 1834 novel The Last Days of Pompeii is public domain; this game does not adapt it.
PRG32 framework and its portable cartridge ABI.
content_notice: Mild fantasy combat with a staff against looters; a historical natural disaster is depicted without casualties.

controls.action: Move, relative to the camera; circle the target while focused; tibia notes
Strike looters and fallen rubble; advance dialogue
Context action: rescue, read, check; lower the tibia
Raise the tibia; play notes with UP, LEFT, RIGHT, DOWN and A
Focus on the nearest looter or object; with nothing near, recenter the camera
Start; rise again after defeat; new game after the ending
